Cyclical

/SIK-lih-kuhl/ - the stress falls on SIK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cyclical means occurring in repeating cycles or regularly recurring patterns.

The bay's crab harvest is cyclical, fat seasons and lean ones taking turns in a rhythm the old captains can feel coming.

Worked Example

In the far north, lemming populations boom and bust on a beat of roughly four years, and the snowy owls that eat them boom and bust a step behind. Field notebooks going back a century of winters trace the same rising and falling line again and again: the system is cyclical, and the birds are bound to it as tightly as the seasons.

Cyclical is the exact word because it names what occurs in repeating cycles or regularly recurring patterns — movement that swings away and comes back on a rhythm. Recurring says only that a thing happens again; cyclical adds the shape of the loop, the swing away and back that a graph shows tracing itself over and over.

How Cyclical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

recurring

recurring: happening again and again, with no claim of rhythm

rhythmic

rhythmic: steady as a drumbeat; cyclical loops can take years to come around once

Antonyms

linear

linear: running in one direction, never returning

one-off

one-off: happening a single time

How Strong Is It? — recurring → cyclical → metronomic

recurring vs. cyclical

recurring vs. cyclical: A recurring problem simply keeps showing up; cyclical promises a shaped loop — away, back, and away again on a rhythm.

metronomic vs. cyclical

metronomic vs. cyclical: Metronomic goes past cyclical — the return is not just regular but machine-exact, tick after identical tick.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cycl

Root — cycl: circle, wheel (Greek kyklos)

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Cycl (circle, wheel) + -ical (relating to) = relating to a circle. Greek kyklos is the wheel behind bicycle and cyclone alike. Cyclical borrows the wheel and rolls it through time: events that ride a circle come back around to where they began, and then set off again.

Use the root in a new word: recycle

Use the root in a new word: recycle: Glass that is recycled is sent around the circle again to be made into something new.

Word Choice

neutral / analytic

Reach for cyclical when a pattern swings away and reliably comes back around. Its neighbors in this unit divide the territory: sequential orders steps in a line that runs once; sporadic scatters events with no rhythm at all; and when the sameness has merely gone dull, the complaint you want is monotonous.
